chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who divorces his wife while he is absent from her: from which day does she observe the waiting period? He said: If a just testimony is presented that she was divorced on a known day, she shall observe the waiting period from the day she was divorced. And if she does not remember which day and which month, she shall observe the waiting period from the day the news reaches her.
ai.seo_question: When does a divorced woman's waiting period begin if her husband is absent and the exact date of divorce is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of 'iddah commencement in cases of absent husbands, distinguishing between scenarios with definitive proof of the divorce date versus those relying on the receipt of news. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on evidentiary standards in family law, ensuring fairness by anchoring the waiting period to the actual event when verifiable, rather than the delay in communication.
